source.title: Understanding the Interaction of Adversarial Training with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Jia-Ning Zhu; Jing-Feng Zhang; Bo Han; Tong-Liang Liu; Gang Niu; Hong-Xia Yang; Mohan Kankanhalli; Masashi Sugiyama

record.tranche_reason: Compares training and test accuracy under label noise for standard and adversarial training, bearing conceptually on whether models fit noisy labels while generalization degrades.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses cited results on random-label memorization, but does not itself train on completely random labels. Its own results concern symmetric- and pair-flipping noise. Figure-only values are not reconstructed. The study tests V4 through noisy-label training and test accuracy; the other versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study measures clean-label versus noisy-label learning over training and test accuracy across corruption rates. Its own results bear on V4 and V6; V6 is tested directly, not merely cited.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that AT's smoothing effects distinguish correct from incorrect data and alleviate noisy-label memorization. They also propose PGD-step count for distinguishing label quality and typicality, with applications to robust annotation and confidence scores. The mitigation is stronger on MNIST; noisy labels still harm CIFAR-10.
record.recipe_differences: Studies noisy labels in standard and adversarial training, rather than the original random-label fitting setup; the main experiments use ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and SmallCNN on MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with training method (ST versus AT), dataset (CIFAR-10 versus MNIST), noise type, and noise rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Neighborhood prediction entropy, loss-landscape smoothness, geometry-based sample stratification, and robust-annotator performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AT smooths predictions around mislabeled examples, and PGD attack difficulty can identify label quality and annotation confidence.

record.problems: The study tests selected partial-noise rates rather than the full range through all labels corrupted. Results in the cited figures are mostly plotted, with no exact values reported in the text. The training accuracy measure is split by correct/incorrect examples rather than reporting exact overall training error.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error under that condition, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence slowing with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Corruption beyond 0.4 through fully randomized labels, progression to chance test performance, and numerically established perfect training fit across the sweep.
Ablations establishing the necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation.
Completely randomized datasets and direct identification of shared internal representations; the measured evidence concerns learning order for clean and corrupted subsets.

missing.what: Explicit early clean-label advantage and rapid later incorrect-label learning under ST, contrasted with slower incorrect-label learning under AT. Add separate trajectory rows for V6.

Training and test accuracy at additional symmetric-flipping rates 0.1 and 0.3, and pair-flipping rates 0.1–0.4. AT retains clean/noisy separation; ST test degradation increases with noise. Preserve noise types as separate conditions.
missing.versions: V4, V6 where learning trajectories are readable

missing.what: Architecture comparisons: ResNet-10/18/26/34 at 20% symmetric noise, and WRN-32-10 test trajectories under symmetric and pair-flipping noise. The authors report persistent AT mitigation across these networks.

record.verdict_notes: No exact curve values can be recovered from the supplied text. Clean/noisy accuracy equality is insufficient to infer zero training error. AT is a change of training objective, so its results qualify scope rather than contradicting the standard-training result.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment with completely random labels or a test-error-at-chance result.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed as label corruption increases.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

Does not test noise rates through all corruption levels; reports selected rates up to 0.4. Does not establish perfect overall training fit, steadily rising test error toward chance, or separate capture of signal from memorization across the full noise range.
No ablation of weight decay, dropout or data augmentation to test their necessity or sufficiency.
Does not measure the order in which real patterns and label noise are learned; this is cited as prior work.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Standard training on CIFAR-10 with symmetric-flipping label noise; measured standard accuracy on correct and incorrect training examples.
rows.measure: Standard training accuracy, separated by correct versus incorrect training labels over epochs.
rows.baseline: AT under the same dataset and noise conditions
rows.value: The accuracy gap between correct and incorrect training data disappears by epoch 100.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Closing the clean/noisy accuracy gap does not establish perfect training fit for V4 without endpoint accuracies. Section 4.1 additionally reports an early clean/noisy gap followed by rapid noisy-label learning after epoch 60, an observed V6 effect. Split endpoint fit and learning order into separate rows because their states differ.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine for perfect training fit. V6: observed when the temporal findings are included: early separation, rapid incorrect-label learning after epoch 60, convergence by epoch 100. Split the version-specific states.
source_check.problem: The shared cannot_determine state misses the V6 learning dynamics explicitly reported in Section 4.1.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Adversarial training on CIFAR-10 with symmetric-flipping label noise; measured standard accuracy on correct and incorrect training examples.
rows.measure: Standard training accuracy, separated by correct versus incorrect training labels over epochs.
rows.baseline: ST under the same dataset and noise conditions
rows.value: At epoch 100, a large performance gap between correct and incorrect training data remains.
rows.note: Shows that AT does not fit incorrect labels as fully as the claim's perfect-fit description implies.
rows.check: AT learns incorrect labels incompletely: their accuracy rises relatively slowly and remains below clean-label accuracy at epoch 100. This qualifies V4 and shows incomplete late noisy-label learning for V6. Include the early-versus-late trajectory from Section 4.1.

source_check.correct: V4: partial because incorrect training labels remain less completely fitted. V6: observed learning-order evidence; incorrect-label accuracy rises relatively slowly after epoch 60 and remains below correct-label accuracy at epoch 100.
source_check.problem: Partial fits V4, but a persistent gap does not establish incomplete V6 ordering.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Standard training on CIFAR-10; measured standard accuracy on natural test data under symmetric-flipping label noise.
rows.measure: Standard accuracy on natural test data over epochs.
rows.value: Test accuracy first increases and then decreases; larger noise rates cause more serious drops, especially later in training.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative trend; plotted numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: The measured component behaves as V4 predicts: higher tested corruption rates cause larger test-accuracy losses. Lack of a full corruption sweep is an untested part, not evidence that this measured effect is partial.

source_check.locator_found: Introduction; Figure 4(a); Section 4.2; Appendix B.1, Result 2.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Adversarial training on CIFAR-10; measured standard accuracy on natural test data under symmetric-flipping label noise.
rows.measure: Standard accuracy on natural test data over epochs.
rows.baseline: Noise rate 0.0 and ST under corresponding noise conditions
rows.value: AT alleviates the negative effects of label noise; the text says there is no obvious overfitting phenomenon.
rows.note: The text says incorrect data still have some negative impact on AT for CIFAR-10.
rows.check: Separate noise-rate dependence from overfitting over epochs. Appendix B.1 explicitly reports lower AT test accuracy with greater noise, although temporal overfitting is weak. Mitigation does not establish an absent or reversed noise-rate effect.

source_check.locator_found: Figure 4(a); Section 4.2; paragraph following Figure 5; Appendix B.1, Result 2.

rows.subject: SmallCNN
rows.operation_detail: Standard training on MNIST; measured standard accuracy on correct and incorrect training examples under symmetric-flipping label noise.
rows.measure: Standard training accuracy, separated by correct versus incorrect training labels over epochs.
rows.baseline: AT under the same dataset and noise conditions
rows.value: The ST accuracy gap between correct and incorrect training data disappears by epoch 100.
rows.note: The text says the gap is more obvious on MNIST than CIFAR-10 before it disappears in ST.
rows.check: Equal clean/noisy endpoint accuracies alone do not establish perfect training fit for V4. Section 4.1 reports early separation and later rapid noisy-label learning, an observed V6 effect. Split endpoint fit and learning order into separate rows.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine for perfect training fit. V6: observed when early separation and later rapid incorrect-label learning from Section 4.1 are included. Split the version-specific states.
source_check.problem: The shared cannot_determine state misses the reported V6 dynamics.

rows.subject: SmallCNN
rows.operation_detail: Adversarial training on MNIST; measured standard accuracy on correct and incorrect training examples under symmetric-flipping label noise.
rows.measure: Standard training accuracy, separated by correct versus incorrect training labels over epochs.
rows.baseline: ST under the same dataset and noise conditions
rows.value: A large accuracy gap between correct and incorrect training data remains at epoch 100.
rows.note: The result concerns partitioned training accuracy, not exact overall training error.
rows.check: AT retains a clean/noisy accuracy gap and learns incorrect labels relatively slowly. Include the temporal result from Section 4.1; the persistent endpoint gap alone does not describe learning order.

source_check.correct: V4: partial because incorrect-label fitting remains below correct-label fitting. V6: observed learning-order evidence; incorrect labels are learned relatively slowly and the gap remains at epoch 100.
source_check.problem: Partial is appropriate for V4, but the persistent gap does not contradict V6's learning order.

rows.subject: SmallCNN
rows.operation_detail: Standard training on MNIST; measured standard accuracy on natural test data under symmetric-flipping label noise.
rows.measure: Standard accuracy on natural test data over epochs.
rows.value: Larger noise rates cause test accuracy to drop more seriously in ST.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative trend; plotted numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: The reported test-accuracy degradation with increased corruption supports the measured component of V4. Perfect training fit and degradation toward chance remain unestablished.

rows.subject: SmallCNN
rows.operation_detail: Adversarial training on MNIST; measured standard accuracy on natural test data under symmetric-flipping label noise.
rows.measure: Standard accuracy on natural test data over epochs.
rows.baseline: Noise rate 0.0 and ST under corresponding noise conditions
rows.value: AT alleviates the negative effects of noise; the paper says performance can be similar to noise-free training on MNIST.
rows.note: This does not establish a smooth progression to chance test performance.
rows.check: The test-accuracy effect is greatly attenuated under AT on MNIST. Similarity to noise-free performance is qualitative; the text does not establish zero noise dependence.

relationships.reason: R3 and R7 report greater test-accuracy degradation with greater corruption; R1 and R5 report eventual clean/noisy accuracy convergence, although perfect fit is not established.
relationships.display_finding: Greater corruption caused greater test accuracy degradation, while accuracy on clean and noisy training examples eventually converged.

tranche.reason: The study directly compares noisy-label learning under standard and adversarial training using training and test accuracy.

source_check.notes: Exact endpoint accuracies are not stated in the prose. Checks of combined synthesis statements cover this study's ST/AT findings only; the separate 80% sweep, TRADES, and other named interventions are not results established by this text.

statements.correction: Section 4.1: ST incorrect-label accuracy increases rapidly after epoch 60; AT incorrect-label accuracy rises relatively slowly; AT retains a gap at epoch 100. V6 specifies learning order, not complete eventual fitting or closure of the gap.
statements.problem: The dynamics and epoch are correct, but interpreting incomplete endpoint memorization as a limitation of V6 adds a requirement that V6 does not state.
